name: Rasayel
tagline: A small, 27-person WhatsApp sales-and-support platform with a genuinely excellent Shopify integration — real order creation and refunds directly over WhatsApp — held back by weak reporting.
tldr: Rasayel was founded by a team spanning Ireland and Egypt, with sources conflicting on the exact year (2020 vs 2022), is headquartered in Alberta, Canada while operating remotely, and has a lean team of 27 employees.

Pricing runs Start $30/user/mo, Grow $40/user/mo (some sources cite minimum seat requirements of 5-10 users, meaning a realistic minimum monthly spend of $150-360), with Enterprise starting at $2,000/month billed annually.

The Shopify integration is a genuine standout, among the deepest found in this entire comparison set: merchants can sync orders, create new orders, view order history, and issue refunds directly over WhatsApp, not just look up order status.

Integration breadth extends well beyond Shopify — native HubSpot and Pipedrive CRM integrations, plus Zapier connectivity to 5,000+ other apps, giving Rasayel genuinely broad reach for a company this size.

Review sentiment is strong (4.7/5 on Capterra, 4.5/5 on G2), with the shared team inbox and lead-qualification automation specifically praised, but real, repeated complaints describe weak reporting (making it hard to measure customer satisfaction), a cluttered interface, and occasional bugs opening individual chats.

Best for small-to-mid B2B sales teams and Shopify merchants wanting genuinely deep WhatsApp commerce capability and CRM connectivity — not for teams that need robust built-in reporting or a highly polished, uncluttered interface out of the box.

faq.question: How deep is Rasayel's Shopify integration?
faq.answer: Genuinely deep, among the strongest in this entire comparison set: merchants can sync existing orders, create new orders, view full order history, and issue refunds — all directly over WhatsApp, without switching to the Shopify admin. This is real write-access commerce capability, not just an order-status lookup, comparable in depth to dedicated ecommerce specialists like Gorgias or Re:amaze.

faq.question: How much does Rasayel actually cost?
faq.answer: Start is $30/user/month and Grow is $40/user/month, though some sources describe minimum seat requirements (5-10 users depending on the source), meaning a realistic minimum monthly cost of $150-360 rather than a single-seat entry price. Enterprise starts at $2,000/month billed annually for larger deployments. Confirm the current minimum seat requirement directly, since sources disagree on the exact figure.

faq.question: What's the most common complaint about Rasayel?
faq.answer: Reporting and analytics, specifically. Independent reviewers describe a lack of a good reporting tool as making it genuinely hard to measure customer satisfaction, alongside separate complaints about a cluttered, not-very-user-friendly interface and occasional bugs preventing a chat from opening with a specific contact.

faq.question: Does Rasayel integrate with CRM tools beyond Shopify?
faq.answer: Yes — native HubSpot and Pipedrive integrations are documented, and a Zapier connection reaches 5,000+ additional apps for broader no-code automation. This is genuinely wide integration coverage for a company with only 27 employees.

faq.question: Does Rasayel support channels beyond WhatsApp?
faq.answer: Yes — Telegram, Facebook Messenger, Viber, and SMS are all documented native channels alongside WhatsApp, unified in one shared team inbox, which is broader coverage than several other WhatsApp-focused competitors of similar size.

faq.question: How sophisticated is Rasayel's AI chatbot?
faq.answer: Real but modestly documented — a no-code chatbot builder with an AI-assisted instant-response capability, praised by some reviewers, but without the technical specificity (named training methods, resolution benchmarks) that more AI-forward competitors publish. No independently audited resolution-rate figure exists.

pricingBreakdown: Rasayel's per-user pricing ($30-40/user/month) looks competitive at first glance, but the real entry cost depends heavily on minimum seat requirements that different sources describe inconsistently — one citing a 5-user minimum, another a 10-seat minimum working out to $360/month. That's a meaningful gap for a small team trying to budget precisely, and worth confirming directly rather than assuming the lowest published per-user rate applies to a 1-2 person team. The jump to Enterprise at $2,000/month billed annually is a steep cliff from the per-user tiers, suggesting Rasayel's mid-market pricing is genuinely aimed at small-to-mid teams rather than solo operators or the largest enterprises. Given the platform's genuine strength in Shopify commerce integration, a merchant doing real order volume through WhatsApp may find the per-user cost justified by the depth of what the Shopify integration alone delivers.

verdict: Rasayel's Shopify integration is the reason to seriously consider this product, and it's genuinely one of the deepest I've found across this entire comparison set: real order creation, order history, and refund processing happen directly inside WhatsApp conversations, not just a status lookup bolted onto a chat widget. That commerce depth is backed by real integration breadth beyond Shopify too — native HubSpot and Pipedrive connections plus Zapier's reach into 5,000+ other apps give a 27-person company more integration surface area than several larger, better-funded competitors in this category. The shared team inbox and automated lead-qualification workflows are similarly well-reviewed, with reviewers specifically crediting the automation for real reductions in manual workload rather than vague productivity claims. Where Rasayel genuinely falls short, and independent reviewers are specific and consistent about this, is reporting: a documented lack of good reporting tools makes it hard to measure customer satisfaction, and the interface itself is described as cluttered rather than polished, with occasional bugs preventing individual chats from opening. Pricing also requires more diligence than the headline per-user rate suggests, since sources disagree on minimum seat requirements. My honest read: if Rasayel's Shopify commerce depth and broad CRM integration match your actual workflow, and you don't have a hard requirement for robust built-in reporting, this is a genuinely capable, well-reviewed small-team product worth serious evaluation. If measuring CSAT and having a polished interface matter as much as the underlying capability, test both directly during a trial before committing.
